meta.title: Squad · Manager–worker coordination
meta.subtitle: CLI invocations coordinate through local SQLite state — agents execute the work, not Squad

components.label: Manager agent
components.explanation: A role prompt, not a privileged scheduler. The manager joins, checks agents, creates a tracked assignment, and receives replies. It can inspect task list for persisted results. Review by an inspector is an agent convention outside this focused view, not a task-state gate enforced by the CLI.

components.label: Worker agent
components.explanation: The worker receives an assignment, explicitly acknowledges it, performs work in its own agent environment, then completes the task with a summary. A separate send can report the result to the manager. Squad does not execute the task body in this CLI path.

components.label: Squad CLI
components.explanation: Each terminal invokes the same binary independently. It discovers .squad by walking parent directories and opens .squad/messages.db. join registers an agent and prints its role prompt (custom .squad/roles/<role>.md overrides built-ins). send, receive and task create/ack/complete check active identity and session tokens. receive emits text or JSON; --wait holds an exclusive per-agent lock, polls unread messages every 500 ms, and touches last_seen every 30 seconds. A missing local session token is accepted for compatibility, so this is not strong authentication.

components.label: Store · rusqlite
components.explanation: create_task requires active creator and assignee; one SQLite transaction inserts a queued task and an unread task_assigned message. ack_task requires queued state and matching assignee, then sets acked with lease_owner and a 15-minute lease timestamp. complete_task requires acked state and matching lease_owner, then stores completed and result_summary; it inserts no result message and does not test lease expiry. receive_messages transactionally selects unread messages for a recipient and marks them read; delivery is distinct from task acknowledgement. Freeform sends insert notes; @all fans out to active agents except the sender.

components.label: Session + wait files
components.explanation: Session helpers write/read/delete .squad/sessions/<agent-id> tokens. receive --wait creates locks/<agent-id>.receive.lock under the workspace root, not inside .squad, and keeps an fs2 exclusive lock for the wait loop. This prevents concurrent waiters for the same agent; it does not serialize all CLI commands.

components.label: .squad/messages.db
components.explanation: Shared local coordination state across CLI invocations. agents stores roles, session tokens, presence and active/archived status. messages stores recipient, sender, content, read flag, kind and optional task_id/reply_to. tasks stores creator, assignee, status, lease fields and result_summary. Message reads retain rows; history can show read and unread messages. No remote message broker is on this path.

cards.title: Assignment → execution
items: create: queued task + assignment message commit together
receive: mark message read ≠ task ack
ack: queued → acked; complete: acked → completed

cards.title: How the manager gets the result
items: complete persists result_summary; no automatic result message
Manager uses task list, or worker sends a separate note
Freeform send / receive uses the same persisted message table

cards.title: Boundaries of this implementation
items: Roles guide agents; no manager-only authorization gate
15-minute lease timestamp is not enforced by complete
Requeue resets task state; it emits no new assignment message
